story: My landlord in Delhi says the law lets him keep my Rs 50,000 deposit forever because I left before 11 months. Is that the law?

timeline.event: Landlord claims they can keep the deposit forever because the user left before 11 months.
timeline.user_words: My landlord in Delhi says the law lets him keep my Rs 50,000 deposit forever because I left before 11 months. Is that the law?

facts.user_goal: To understand if the landlord is legally allowed to keep the deposit forever for leaving before 11 months, and likely to get the deposit back.

rules.message: Deposit refunds depend on your State's rent law and your rent agreement. I haven't verified any State rent law yet, so I won't quote one. I can still help you write a demand letter based on your facts. Free legal aid (15100) can tell you your State's rule.

rules.name: deposit_limitation
rules.message: I haven't verified the time limit for getting a deposit back through court, so I won't guess one. Don't wait - a lawyer can confirm it quickly.

answer.summary: Your landlord cannot legally keep your Rs 50,000 deposit forever just because you left early. The landlord must return your deposit as per your rent agreement and state law. If your landlord does not return it, you can take legal action. You can also get free legal help to understand your exact rights.

claims.text: Your landlord cannot legally keep your Rs 50,000 deposit forever just because you left early.
The landlord must return your deposit as per your rent agreement and state law.

next_steps.action: Keep all your rent receipts, the rent agreement, and messages with your landlord safe.
next_steps.why: You will need these as proof that you paid the deposit and that the landlord agreed to return it.

Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for return of security deposit

I paid you a security deposit of Rs 50,000 on [FILL: date paid] for the premises at [FILL: address]. [FILL: the date you vacated and handed over the keys - only if you have moved out] The deposit has not been returned.

I request you to return the deposit, less any deduction you can justify in writing with bills, within 15 days of receiving this letter.

If it is not returned, I will take legal action to recover it, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: [FILL: receipts, chats, emails, bank statements].

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]
draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in your rent agreement.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: none - this letter states facts only
